feedback: Correct. The 3-state counter faithfully captures 'has_key true on >=2 distinct time points': u0 fires to u1 on the first holding move (+0.1), u1 fires to u2 on the second (+1.0), and u2 absorbs. Because transitions fire once per time step, consecutive holds (pickup then keep carrying) and the drop/re-pickup variant (pickup, drop -> key_lost else-loop in u1, pickup) both reach u2 exactly when the task is done, matching the seed-1 variant trace. FINAL_STATES header present with u2 declared and accepting. Transition function is total: per-state else self-loops cover all irrelevant combinations (door_open, at_goal, key_lost, and has_key in u2), so no unordered event can derail the count. has_key is correctly treated as a persistent condition (fires every step it holds), which is what the counting task requires; the key_lost event is rightly unused. Rewards are non-negative, monotone (0.1 < 1.0), bounded (total 1.1; no transition can be re-fired for repeated reward since u0 and u1 are left permanently and u2 self-loops at 0), and there is no hacking path: the only route to u2 requires two distinct has_key steps, which is exactly the task, so the RM accepts precisely the satisfying traces. The property is monotone, so no regression transitions are needed. Format matches the paper template (STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION, else-labels, implicit zero rewards on unlisted self-loops).

The truthiness guard on previous_valuation is harmless and cannot mask a true prior valuation, since a complete non-empty valuation dict is truthy. No imports, no actions, no mutation of the environment or episode memory; all functions are pure, syntactically valid, and return proper booleans. Grid scans guard empty cells with 'cell is not None' before attribute access, and env.grid.get(*env.agent_pos) is a safe unpack of the documented (x, y) tuple. Runtime and semantic alignment with the DoorKey environment is sound.
